title: Kummer etale G-covers and their quotients after fs base change
statement:
Let $C,D,E$ be locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $G$ be a finite group of order invertible on $D$, and let $q:C\to D$ be a Kummer etale $G$-cover. Here Kummer etale means log etale [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] with injective characteristic monoid maps for which every element of the target has a positive multiple in the image. A $G$-cover means that $G$ acts over $D$, $q$ is finite surjective, and the canonical map $\coprod_{g\in G}C\to C\times_D^{\rm fs}C$, given on the $g$th copy by $(1,g)$, is an isomorphism. The superscript fs denotes the fibre product in the category of fs log schemes. For any morphism $E\to D$ for which $C_E=C\times_D^{\rm fs}E$ is locally Noetherian, $C_E\to E$ is again a Kummer etale $G$-cover. Its underlying scheme has quotient $E$: the map is finite surjective with orbit geometric fibres and
$$\mathcal O_E\simeq(q_{E*}\mathcal O_{C_E})^G.$$
The quotient log structure is $M_E\simeq(q_{E*}M_{C_E})^G$. The constructions and identifications commute with composition of fs base changes. No flatness of $E\to D$ and no triviality of its log structure is assumed. In particular, the very tame finite quotient of [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient], when the action is free on the log-triviality locus, is a Kummer etale $G$-cover in this sense, so these conclusions apply to its fs base changes.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, p.125, fs-cartesian diagram; X 1.8, pp.146--147, diagram (1.a) and the explicit assertion that Kummer etale G-covers are stable under any fs base change; VI Theorem 3.2, p.73.

proof.text: Write $C_E=C\times_D^{\rm fs}E$. Every ordinary fibre product below is finite over a locally Noetherian scheme, since $q$ is finite and finiteness is stable under base change [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], hence locally Noetherian, so these fs products exist. The fs-product universal property in [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison] defines $g_E$ by the pair $(g,1_E)$ for every $g\in G$. The identity and multiplication rules hold because their two projections agree, so these maps give an action over $E$. Associating iterated fs products identifies $C_E\times_E^{\rm fs}C_E$ with $(C\times_D^{\rm fs}C)\times_D^{\rm fs}E$: both represent pairs of maps to $C$ with equal composite to $D$, together with a compatible map to $E$. A finite disjoint union of fs log schemes is their scheme disjoint union with the component log structures; pulling it back simply pulls back each open-and-closed component. Thus base change of the assumed diagonal isomorphism is exactly $\coprod_{g\in G}C_E\xrightarrow{(1,g_E)}C_E\times_E^{\rm fs}C_E$.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.146--147, fs-cartesian diagram (1.a); universal-property argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-kummer-etale-fs-base-change-stability] to $q$ and $E\to D$. Both schemes are locally Noetherian by hypothesis, and the ordinary product $C\times_DE$ is locally Noetherian by Step 1. It gives log etaleness and the Kummer condition for $q_E:C_E\to E$.

source.place: X 1.8, p.147, stability under any fs base change

proof.text: By [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison], the comparison $C_E\to C\times_DE$ is finite and surjective, since $q$ is Kummer. The ordinary projection $C\times_DE\to E$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]; finiteness of their composite follows from the same statement. Its surjectivity can be checked at an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ over a point of $E$: the nonempty finite fibre of $C\to D$ remains nonempty over $\Omega$, since its residue fields embed into $\Omega$ over the prescribed residue field. Surjectivity of the comparison then gives a point of $C_E$ above that point. Thus $q_E$ is finite surjective. Here neither projection is assumed to be flat.

source.place: X 1.8, p.147; finite fs comparison and ordinary finite base change

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar e$ of $E$, and pull back strictly to $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{E,\bar e}$. The strict local ring is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. Ordinary products over $T$ of schemes finite over $T$ are finite over $T$, hence Noetherian. By [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison], strict pullback is the ordinary scheme pullback; it is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and Kummer etale by [lem-per-kummer-etale-fs-base-change-stability]. Apply [lem-per-kummer-strict-local-standard-model] to $C_E\times_ET\to T$, obtaining connected strictly local components $V_i$ with standard groups $\Gamma_i$. For any $i,j$, $V_i\times_T^{\rm fs}V_j$ is nonempty: the ordinary product is nonempty (both have a point over the closed point), and its fs comparison is surjective by [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison]. Step 1's diagonal isomorphism therefore forces some $g\in G$ to carry $V_i$ to $V_j$. If $H$ stabilizes $V_i$, restrict that isomorphism to $V_i\times_T^{\rm fs}V_i$. It becomes $\coprod_{h\in H}V_i\simeq V_i\times_T^{\rm fs}V_i$. Every $h$ is a unique character automorphism by the standard-model node. Comparing with its canonical decomposition into $\Gamma_i$ copies of the connected $V_i$ shows that $H\to\Gamma_i$ is bijective, and it is a homomorphism because it is the action map.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72, standard local charts and Galois fs diagonal

proof.text: For a transitive $G$-permutation of components, evaluation on component $i$ identifies invariant tuples with $H$-invariant sections there: the inverse sends $s$ to its translates, independently of representatives of $G/H$ because $s$ is $H$-fixed. Step 4 identifies $H$ with $\Gamma_i$, so both invariant-sheaf equalities of [lem-per-kummer-strict-local-standard-model] identify these local invariants with $\mathcal O_T$ and $M_T$. To read this at the original stalk $\bar e$, use [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-pushforward-stalk] for the underlying sheaves of sets of $\mathcal O_{C_E}$ and $M_{C_E}$: their pushforward stalks are precisely the products of the geometric stalks of these components. Invariants commute with taking such stalks: represent a fixed germ on a neighbourhood, then shrink for each of the finitely many equations $g(s)=s$ to a common neighbourhood; equality of two germs is handled by the same shrinking. This proves the canonical ring and monoid maps are bijective at every $\bar e$. By [lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] they are isomorphisms of sheaves, respecting structure maps and units since all maps are the original log pullbacks.

source.place: VI 2.3, p.73, the two invariant-sheaf identities; geometric stalk descent

proof.text: Each strictly local component in Step 4 has just one closed geometric point over $\bar e$. The transitivity proved there says exactly that the geometric fibres of $q_E$ are $G$-orbits. The invariant ring formula of Step 5 also proves the scheme quotient assertion locally: for an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset E$, finiteness makes $q_E^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine, and the formula gives $A=B^G$. Apply [lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient] to this Noetherian affine source: it is Noetherian because $U$ is Noetherian and the map finite, and all stabilizer orders divide the invertible $|G|$. Its quotient is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}B^G=U$. These local categorical quotients agree on overlaps by their uniqueness and hence give the quotient $E$ globally. The log quotient is the invariant log structure already identified in Step 5.

source.place: VI 2.3, p.73, standard quotients; VI 3.2, p.74, admissible scheme quotient

proof.text: For the final application take the quotient $C\to D$ of [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient], retaining the standing invertibility assumption on $|G|$. It gives a finite surjective Kummer etale map between log regular schemes. Over the strict localization $T$ at $\bar d$, [lem-per-kummer-strict-local-standard-model] gives strictly local standard components $V_i$. Geometric orbit fibres of the quotient imply that $G$ permutes these components transitively. Fix one, with inertia group $H$ and standard sharp chart $P\to Q$. By [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants], its strict local log stalk $M$ satisfies $M_{D,\bar d}=M^H$. Write $K=Q^{\rm gp}/P^{\rm gp}$, choose $n>0$ invertible in the base annihilating $K$, and put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mu_n)$. The standard-model node identifies every log automorphism over $T$ with a unique member of $\Gamma$. Consequently the actual action gives a homomorphism $H\to\Gamma$; no equivariance of an independently chosen standard chart has been assumed.

source.place: VI 3.5(a)--(c), pp.74--76, equivariant standard strict-local quotient chart

proof.text: The strict-local components in Step 7 are log regular: their map to $C$ is the ordinary base change of a strict localization, and [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies their strict local rings and pulled-back log stalks with those of $C$. Thus the stratum and dimension conditions persist. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], their triviality loci are nonempty. The kernel of $H\to\Gamma$ acts identically on a component; freeness on its triviality locus forces this kernel to be trivial. Let $J$ be the image in $\Gamma$. To show its annihilator in $K$ is zero, represent a class by $q_1-q_2$ with $q_1,q_2\in Q$. Since $nq_2\in P$, the same class is represented by $q=q_1+(n-1)q_2\in Q$. If $J$ annihilates it, the chart section $z^q$ in the log stalk is $H$-fixed. The equality $M_{D,\bar d}=M^H$ of Step 7 says it descends to a base log germ. On sharp characteristics this says $q\in P$, so the class is zero. By [lem-per-finite-character-annihilator-duality], $J=\Gamma$, hence $H\simeq\Gamma$. The standard diagonal of [lem-per-kummer-strict-local-standard-model] is therefore the actual $H$-diagonal. Transitivity of the components then shows, as in Step 4, that the $G$-diagonal of $C\times_DT\to T$ is an isomorphism.

It remains to globalize Step 8. Let $\delta:\coprod_{g\in G}C\to C\times_D^{\rm fs}C$ be the $G$-diagonal. Its source is finite over $D$, and so is its target by [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison] and [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Its base change along the strict map $T\to D$ at any geometric point $\bar d$ is the $G$-diagonal of $C\times_DT\to T$, by the strict clause of [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison] and the iterated-product identification of Step 1; Step 8 shows this is an isomorphism of log schemes. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-pushforward-stalk], applied to the structure sheaves, the stalks at $\bar d$ of their pushforwards to $D$ are the products of the strict local rings over the geometric points above $\bar d$, i.e. the coordinate rings of these base changes to $T$, so $\delta$ induces bijections on them. By [lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] the map of pushforward algebras is an isomorphism, and since both sides are affine over $D$, $\delta$ is an isomorphism of schemes. The log structure map $\delta^{-1}M\to M$ is bijective on the log stalk at every geometric point, which is a log stalk of a component over the corresponding $T$; by [lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] it is an isomorphism. This proves the final application.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72, Galois fs diagonal of the strict-local standard cover; local-to-global by geometric stalks

proof.text: For successive fs base changes $F\to E\to D$, both $(C\times_D^{\rm fs}E)\times_E^{\rm fs}F$ and $C\times_D^{\rm fs}F$ represent the same compatible pairs of maps, so their unique comparison is an isomorphism and respects the $G$-actions. On three successive base changes the two associativity composites have identical projections, hence agree. The invariant ring and log identifications in Step 5 are the canonical pullback maps: composing them sends a section to its successive pullbacks, which equals its direct pullback by functoriality of a log morphism [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Thus the quotient identifications commute with composition. This assertion concerns the resulting fs quotients; it does not identify their underlying schemes with ordinary scheme base changes.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.146--147, functorial fs diagrams; universal property
